text: Owner-ruled kit API design principle (2026-08-14, doc44-judgment D1 note): presets are shorthands, never gates. Everything a preset applies must remain reachable through plain props; a preset that gatekeeps an exclusive feature is a design defect. Applies to the Chip lg-frame preset now and every future preset across both apps. Also being written into the kit guidelines (task #44).

Unneeded checkpoint ceremony at 66% free context: acted on the generic tool-count auto-checkpoint nudge (fires at 30/60/90/120 tools) instead of the ctx-pressure instrument (70/80/90%), which had never fired. The standing rule (rules/communication.md, context-load claims need the instrument) already covers /clear and /compact recommendations; the gap is that tool-count nudges also trigger checkpoint ceremony. Pattern: mechanical nudge treated as evidence of context pressure. Owner corrected: Checkpoint was un-needed, we are at 66% free.

Owner-tagged pattern: inferring the earned/conditional nature of structure even when the provided example is necessarily exhaustive, then implementing that way. A template sketch must show every slot to define them; a faithful implementation treats each slot as conditional on real content and proves it with a collapsed example. Generalizes past PR descriptions: any schema, template, or exhaustive example handed over as spec. Dream question: where else do we treat examples as quotas (report formats, checkpoint sections, briefing tiers) and mechanically fill?
